comment: Defaults of the operator tools. Work-root paths are names under protocol-manifest.json workRoot, else the directory above the main checkout. launch.wrapper and launch.engine resolve relative to the repository root; absent files are refused, never bypassed. Project selection sets live in the project layer. The operator may override sections in local config (shallow merge by section).

heavy.comment: Heavy-run gate (PROTO-DEC-0249 items 2 and 3). A heavy run is a protocol-test internal runner or a direct node --test of the product-real or the product-build test file. nodeVersion is the documented runtime prefix; the queue, the train flag and the run registry (pointer files that attribute a live heavy run to its tree) live under the work root.

cleanup.comment: Landing cleanup (PROTO-DEC-0249 item 4). archiveRoot is an absolute directory outside the working tree or null (then the archive goes under the work root); the inventory file older than inventoryMaxHours is refused; a temp root of an ended seat is removed only after tempRetentionDays. A tree whose path matches ownerSessionPattern belongs to a session the owner runs by hand and is never removed; protectedBranches are never deleted (the base branch of the line is protected as well).

loops.comment: LOOP-RUNNER (P-213): supervision of the operator loops through .ai/bin/ops-tools/loops.cjs and the policy .ai/bin/lib/loop-supervisor.cjs. stateDir is one safe name under the work root holding the loop-runner/1 records, locks, launch tokens and logs. commands declares one argv per loop id; tokens carry no shell metacharacters and the last token is a relative script path resolved strictly inside the work root. The shipped defaults declare no commands: the loop commands of a host are scripts of that host outside the product, so they belong in the host or local layer (the local config under the work root), never in the shipped defaults; an undeclared loop is refused with LOOP-UNDECLARED.

legacy.comment: The old file names of the untracked operator tools. A forwarding stub is written only by an explicit --write run; the tool never overwrites a real implementation without --force.
